### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **28** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/package.json`, `packages/runtime/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e098ff46dec6fc0f02fe0776cedfa6189d651e14`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/package.json`, `packages/runtime/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **214** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **154** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **154**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **99** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e098ff46dec6fc0f02fe0776cedfa6189d651e14` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `35e4f231acd746dd0bf6b541424377e134eed6a2` — the merge of head `40a37314195729e9336ee7247401a7e90e903570` into base `e098ff46dec6fc0f02fe0776cedfa6189d651e14`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 35e4f231acd746dd0bf6b541424377e134eed6a2 && git checkout 35e4f231acd746dd0bf6b541424377e134eed6a2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e098ff46dec6fc0f02fe0776cedfa6189d651e14 40a37314195729e9336ee7247401a7e90e903570 && git checkout -B drift-repro e098ff46dec6fc0f02fe0776cedfa6189d651e14 && git merge --no-ff 40a37314195729e9336ee7247401a7e90e903570

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e098ff46dec6fc0f02fe0776cedfa6189d651e14
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e098ff46dec6fc0f02fe0776cedfa6189d651e14` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `40a37314195729e9336ee7247401a7e90e903570`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/domains/permission-set-clone.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/new-similar-target.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/permission-set-clone.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/permission-set-clone-door.dogfood.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts, packages/runtime/package.json, packages/runtime/vitest.config.ts, pnpm-lock.yaml, scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-customization-package.ts (the ensure door), packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-writability.ts (`isWritablePackage`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`saveMetaItem`, `permissionSetOwnerBindingRefusal`), packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts (`resolvePackageClosure`, `narrowObjectsToPackageClosure`), packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts (the ensure HTTP door, `requireDuplicableSource`), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (`errorFromThrown`), packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, docs/adr/0146 D3/D4/D6, and the flow-clone branch `claude/project-thread-sdqbrt` at its current head (`71dca746`) for the shared helper and the four shared config hunks. The prose faces (`.changeset/**`, `content/docs/**`) are read against the diff below but are the lane seat's ACCEPT, not this record's scope. Face: `record-recognisers --paths` on the PR's file list decides no path face (no published schema, no governed path) and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries the `(narrowing)` arm, so the narrowing face alone is owed and this record covers it in full; no further face.

### ① Derived judgments

**The accept set, before and after, at `POST /security/permission-sets/:name/clone` — read off the handler, not the body text.**

1. **`package` omitted, source shipped by a read-only package X (the narrowing).** Before: every such copy answered 200 and was saved package-less. Now `resolveDefaultCloneLanding` calls `protocol.ensureCustomizationPackage({ basePackageId: X })` and the save carries the pair as its own `packageId`. The inputs that move from accept to refuse are exactly the ensure door's own refusals, read in `ensurePairOnce` on `main`: X declares no namespace, or its namespace has no valid pair namespace (too long, invalid) → 409; the pair is absent and X's version is not SemVer → 409; another package already owns X's pair namespace → 422 `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`; an installed `X.custom` that lacks the namespace or the dependency on X → 409; X's id yields no valid pair id → 400; no package registry → 503; the pair's own install refused by the ADR-0141 D2 dependency check (a base at a prerelease version) → 422 `DEPENDENCY_MISSING` (the class declares status and code itself). One more, in a non-standard composition only: a protocol with `saveMetaItem` but no `ensureCustomizationPackage` → 501 (before: a package-less save). Correct: a refused pair means the copy has nowhere to land that D3/D6 admit, and a package-less fallback would be the second destination the unblock forbids. The PR body and changeset name the three common ones (no namespace, non-SemVer version, namespace owned elsewhere) and say "the ensure door's own sentence"; that is a true and sufficient summary of this list.
2. **No new error code.** The wire codes are: 422 `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` and 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` from the shared rule, both in `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`; the ensure door's 422 `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, ledgered; its code-less 409s take the dispatcher's status-derived code through `deps.errorFromThrown(err, 500)` — the same path the HTTP ensure door (`packages.ts`) answers them through, so the two doors answer one refusal with one envelope. `DUPLICATE_SOURCE_NOT_A_BASE` is deliberately not reused, and the helper's header says why (that code judges a SOURCE, these refusals judge a TARGET); what the card's "family" asks for — the `[tag]` sentence, `packageId` and `docs` in the envelope's details, refuse-before-mutate — is the shape `newSimilarTargetRefusalAnswer` reproduces from `requireDuplicableSource`. Judged right.
3. **Ensure door called in-process, not re-implemented.** The clone door reads `protocol.ensureCustomizationPackage` off the resolved `protocol` service, which on `main` is the class method delegating to `ensureCustomizationPackage.call(host, request)` in `protocol-customization-package.ts`. No pair id, namespace or range is spelled in the runtime; `isWritablePackage` is the one ADR-0070 D2 predicate imported from `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`. The unit suite's ensure double is a model of the contract (created on first call, reused after), and the dogfood drives the real one (404 before the first copy, 200 after; one pair in `GET /packages` after the second). The unblock's "no second creation path" holds.
4. **The row binding goes through the save's package context.** `saveMetaItem({ type, name, item, parentVersion: null, packageId })` — the landing is spread onto the request only when non-null; the item still loses `packageId` through the unchanged `PERMISSION_SET_CLONE_DROPPED_KEYS`. `permissionSetOwnerBindingRefusal` compares a BODY `packageId` with the row's resolved binding and the body has none, so it never fires; the dogfood pins the stored row's `package_id` is the pair while `metadata` has no `packageId`. Correct, and the order's hypothesis is met exactly.
5. **New-name rule and its 409 kept; a set in `.custom` under the base set's name still refused.** Step 5 is unchanged: a name the catalog holds — the source's own included — answers 409 before any landing is resolved or any save attempted; the dogfood's taken-name case still passes. Since the catalog is environment-level and names are unique across packages (D6: one name per deployment), a clone named after its base is refused here regardless of the landing; the clone door does not depend on N-09's save-side refusal (not on `main` yet, PR #28554 being reworked).
6. **Assignable by bare name — the card's unverified item, measured.** The dogfood grants `my_member_default` (asserted bound to the pair) through a position saved by name and resolves it in `resolveUserAuthzGrants`; a new case grants `my_field_ops_delegate` (pair-bound) through a direct `sys_user_permission_set` row, reading it absent first (anti-vacuity). Also measured: the catalog serves the pair-bound copy with `packageId` = pair — the card's other unverified line. Wanted 3 is met by measurement, not assertion.
7. **Walled tenant administrator — both refusals stand.** The clone door asks `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict` then `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` before any read and before the landing step, so under `isolated` / `group` a tenant administrator gets the walled sentence and no pair is ensured (the unit suite now pins `ensures` empty under both postures). The ensure HTTP door keeps its own `requireManageMetadata` plus walled package-write 403 at its own route; the in-process body judges packages only, by its own header, and its authority is the same pair of predicates the clone door asks. No privilege is widened by calling it in-process.
8. **Environment-source control unchanged.** `source.packageId` undefined → `{ packageId: null }`, no ensure, the save's keys exactly as before (`item`, `name`, `parentVersion`, `type`), answer `package: null`; pinned in unit and dogfood.
9. **A source already in a writable package** (an owned base or an existing `.custom`) now lands in that package rather than package-less — a landing change, not a refusal. The ensure door would refuse a writable base 409, so this is the only correct reading. The save into that package is judged by the save door's closure-narrowed gate, the same gate that admitted the source there; I read no practical input this moves to refuse.
10. **`package` given.** Before: 400 (unknown key). Now: a writable installed target whose closure reaches the source's package and every granted object lands there; unknown or read-only (booted code package, or `scope` in the read-only set) → 422 `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` naming the package; closure missing the source's package, or a granted object owned by a package outside the closure → 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`; empty or non-string → 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` on field `package`, never read as omitted. The `objects` limb reuses `narrowObjectsToPackageClosure` with the same four limbs as the save gate (system objects and unpackaged ones admitted; an object no registry holds skipped and left to the save). `permissionSetObjectNames` reads the three places `PermissionSetSchema` names an object (`objects` keys, the object half of `fields` keys, row-level rules' `object`). All judged right; refuse-before-mutate holds (the dogfood checks no catalog entry and no `sys_metadata` row after each refusal).
11. **Answer shape.** `{ permissionSet, package, notice }`, `package` null environment-wide; the notice prefixes a landing sentence to the unchanged `PERMISSION_SET_CLONE_NOTICE`. No ancestry key (ADR-0126 §9) — the copy still names nothing about its source.
12. **The four non-domain files.** `packages/runtime/package.json` + `pnpm-lock.yaml`: a direct `@objectstack/lint` workspace dependency for the two closure walks; `@objectstack/lint` already sits in runtime's closure through `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, and lint depends on neither runtime nor metadata-protocol (deps: formula, sdui-parser, spec), so no cycle and no new install weight. `packages/runtime/vitest.config.ts`: an alias of `@objectstack/lint/runtime` to `../lint/src/runtime.ts`, which `check:test-source-alias` requires once runtime's tests reach that subpath; it makes the tests judge source instead of `dist/`, a strengthening. `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`: one `DISPATCHER_DOMAINS` row declaring `new-similar-target.ts` at `handBuilt: 0`, the strictest count (its one answer goes through `deps.error`); the gate reds on an undeclared domain file, so this is the roster entry a new file owes, not a weakened gate. `scripts/**` is not a governed surface. All four hunks are byte-identical to the flow-clone branch's.
13. **Route-ledger note.** The row stays `server-only` with no `requestSchema`, so Wanted 6's conditional (a Zod request schema in `packages/spec`) is not triggered and none is invented; the note's new sentences (body, landing rules, both refusal codes, the answer's `package`, "the package is the save's own `packageId`, never a key of the item") match the handler line for line.
14. **Docs** (`content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`, `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`): every sentence I checked is true of the code — the two refusal codes, the ensure door as the only creation path, `package: null` environment-wide, assignment by bare name, the dropped-keys list unchanged. Lane seat's ACCEPT confirms the prose; nothing false found here.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the arm `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` defines for exactly this diff — "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another. Both facts are true and both are read": the body gains an optional key and the answer a key (widening), and a request that answered 200 now refuses (narrowing). `Metadata-protocol: none` is honest: no key an author writes, no accepted value and no metadata type changes; an HTTP body key is not metadata, and the copy's stored definition is the same whole-definition copy as before. Per AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 the level follows the kind alone — `none` takes `patch`, "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition" — so `'@objectstack/runtime': patch` is right, the `**BREAKING**` banner is present, and the changeset carries exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a category `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` lists; its reasoning (nothing stored to rewrite, a refused clone writes nothing, the remedy is in the refusal) holds. The PR title's `!` matches. Only `@objectstack/runtime` publishes a changed file (`packages/qa/dogfood` is a test package; `scripts/**`, docs and the changeset ship in no package), so one changeset is the right count.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, "the ensure refusal path is not measured on a live package: no booted package in the showcase or the platform lacks a namespace; the refusal path is the ensure door's own, read from its code." Answered: accepted. The refusal is the ensure door's, pinned by that door's own suite on `main`; the clone door's contribution is passthrough, which `permission-set-clone.test.ts` pins (an ensure throw with status and code reaches the wire unchanged, nothing saved). No escalation.
- Dev `open_questions`: none. `out_of_scope_findings`: `GET /packages/:id/customizations` ledgered but not mounted — this is #28622, main-red since #28595, not this PR's; the dev's dogfood on both the pre-merge and merged heads isolates the one red to that parity file. Carried, not this record's.
- Order's coordination line ("one target rule across the two clone doors, no second spelling; whichever lands first owns the helper"): the dev reports agreement with the #28149 thread and the diff bears it out — `new-similar-target.ts` on this head differs from `claude/project-thread-sdqbrt` at its current head `71dca746` (not only at the `97489b20` the body cites) solely by the `objects` limb: one header paragraph, two optional registry members (`getObject`, `getObjectOwner`), the optional `objects` request field and its block. Signature, codes, statuses, sentences and the `newSimilarTargetRefusalAnswer` shape are byte-identical; the flow door's call (`automation.ts`, passing `target`, `subject`, `sourcePackageId`) compiles against either copy. **What the second-to-land must do:** merge `origin/main` and resolve the add/add conflict on `packages/runtime/src/domains/new-similar-target.ts` by keeping the superset — if this PR lands first, #28621 takes `main`'s file whole (its own is a strict subset) and changes no call site; if #28621 lands first, this PR keeps its own file, which then reads as adding the `objects` limb to the landed helper. The four shared config hunks (`package.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, `check-route-envelope.mjs`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`) are identical on both branches and merge clean. Either order leaves one spelling.
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (the relay), so no login note is owed.
- CI on this head at read time: 30 check-runs succeeded, 27 still in progress, none red; the landing precheck (every check green) is the seat's at arm time, not this record's verdict. `main` is red on the unrelated #28622 (main-red convention: no lane PR arms meanwhile) — that is a landing constraint, not a finding against this diff.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, judged against the published behaviour on `main`: the door advertised a copy "authored in this system: no package" (its docs and ledger note). ADR-0146 D3 ("It receives ... environment-level permission sets for the base (new sets, never an override of the base's — D6)") and D6 ("A customer's own set is a new set in `.custom`") decide the landing; D3 makes the ensure door the only creation path. So the narrowing takes no declared capability away at the consumer — a copy is still made for every source the pair can be ensured for, and the console reads a response that only gained a key — and it makes the ADR's own refusal real where the alternative was a silent second destination. That is the right side of Prime Directive #12: contract-first, no lenient fallback.

Per `Scope` file: `permission-set-clone.ts` holds against the scenario it is accepted on (card Tests, all six measured in dogfood and unit); the step order (authority → walled → shape → body → source → taken name → landing → save) keeps every refusal before any write and the pair un-ensured for a refused caller. `new-similar-target.ts` is pure over the registry, reuses the two lint walks the save gate and Studio's pickers use (one closure for picker and gate, the lint header's own invariant), and its `objects` limb is the right place for a door whose item declares its objects; a flow passes none, as the header states. `route-ledger.ts`, `check-route-envelope.mjs`, `vitest.config.ts`, `package.json`/lockfile: each is the one edit its gate or import requires, none weakens a gate. The tests: the ablation record is credible — the source-package limb's first ablation was green because its only fixture tripped the objects limb too, and the dev added a fixture that isolates the limb before re-running, which is the honest shape.

Two observations, neither a must-fix: (a) the HTTP ensure door answers a prerelease base's refused pair install through `dependencyMissingAnswer` to keep the per-entry `details`; the clone door answers the same throw through `errorFromThrown`, which keeps the status, the code and the `issues` array but not that closed `details` list — the same status and code reach the caller, so the contract holds; a follow-up could share the branch. (b) The default landings (the pair, or the source's own writable package) are not asked the target rule; the save gate's closure judges them, which the dev states in the acceptance notes. Agreed: the pair depends on X by construction and a set already in a package resolved there.
